raw_model_output:
21 CFR Part 820 Subpart Z requires manufacturers to establish and maintain a quality management system that is appropriate for their specific device(s) as described in § 820.1(a). This system must ensure that finished devices are safe and effective and in compliance with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. If a manufacturer engages in only some operations subject to the requirements in this part, it only needs to comply with those applicable to those operations.

Additionally, manufacturers subject to this part must include certain information in records, as outlined in 21 CFR 820.35. This includes information related to control of records, as specified in ISO 13485. Definitions in ISO 13485 and in Clause 3 of ISO 9000 apply to this part, except as specified in paragraph (b) of this section.

Furthermore, manufacturers must document and maintain procedures that provide detailed descriptions of the activities involved in labeling and packaging, as required in 21 CFR 820.45. These procedures must ensure the integrity, inspection, storage, and operations of labeling and packaging during customary conditions of processing, storage, handling, distribution, and use of the device.

If applicable, the requirements in 21 CFR 820.35 apply to the manufacturer's control of records, and the requirements in 21 CFR 820.45 apply to the documentation of labeling and packaging procedures.
